q: Which layer of the OSI model is responsible for routing packets from source host to destination host across networks?
exp: The network layer handles logical addressing and routing of packets between networks.

q: What is the subnet mask corresponding to a /26 prefix?
exp: /26 means 26 network bits: 24 bits + 2 bits of the last octet = 11000000 = 192, so 255.255.255.192.

q: Data bits 1101011 are to be sent using even parity. What should the parity bit be?
exp: The data has five 1s (odd), so a parity bit of 1 makes the total number of 1s even.

q: Which multiplexing technique combines several optical signals of different wavelengths onto a single optical fibre?
exp: Wavelength Division Multiplexing assigns each signal its own light wavelength on the same fibre.

q: In Manchester encoding, every bit period contains
options: a transition only when the bit is 1
a transition only at the end of a 0 bit
a transition in the middle of the bit, which also provides clock synchronisation
no transition at all; the level stays constant
exp: Manchester (IEEE 802.3) is self-clocking: each bit has a mid-bit transition, and its direction gives the bit value. The price is double bandwidth.

q: What is the correct sequence of segments in the TCP three-way handshake?
exp: The client sends SYN, the server replies SYN-ACK, and the client completes with ACK.

q: In a star topology with a central hub, the failure of which component brings down the entire network?
exp: All traffic passes through the hub, so hub failure is a single point of failure for the whole network.

q: A 1500-byte packet is sent over a 10 Mbps link. What is the transmission delay?
exp: Transmission delay = 1500 × 8 bits / 10⁷ bps = 12000 / 10⁷ = 1.2 ms.

q: The IP address 172.20.5.9 belongs to which class?
exp: Class B addresses have first octet in the range 128–191; 172 lies in this range.

q: What is the default port number of HTTPS?
exp: HTTPS uses TCP port 443 by default; HTTP uses 80.

q: In a stop-and-wait protocol, a link has 1 Mbps bandwidth, frames of 1000 bits and one-way propagation delay of 4 ms. What is the link utilization?
exp: Tt = 1 ms, Tp = 4 ms. Utilization = Tt/(Tt + 2Tp) = 1/9 ≈ 11.1%.

q: Which network device forwards frames to a specific port by learning MAC addresses?
exp: A layer-2 switch maintains a MAC address table and forwards frames only to the port of the destination.

q: Which of the following is a lossless data compression technique?
exp: Huffman coding (like RLE and LZW) lets the original data be recovered exactly. JPEG, MP3 and MPEG discard information and are lossy.

q: What is the maximum channel utilization (throughput) of pure ALOHA?
exp: Pure ALOHA maximum throughput is 1/(2e) ≈ 0.184, i.e. 18.4%.

q: Which of the following is a link-state routing protocol?
exp: OSPF floods link-state advertisements and runs Dijkstra's algorithm; RIP and IGRP are distance vector and BGP is path vector.

q: What is the minimum size of an Ethernet frame (IEEE 802.3), including header and CRC?
exp: Minimum Ethernet frame is 64 bytes (46 bytes minimum data plus 18 bytes of header and FCS).

q: Attenuation of a signal over a long cable is overcome by using
options: twisting the wires of the cable
exp: Attenuation is loss of signal strength with distance; amplifiers or repeaters regenerate it. Twisting and shielding reduce crosstalk, and CRC detects errors only.

q: Which OSI layer is concerned with data encryption, compression and translation of data formats?
exp: The presentation layer handles syntax, translation, encryption and compression.

q: How many usable host addresses are available in the network 192.168.10.0/28?
exp: /28 leaves 4 host bits: 2⁴ − 2 = 14 usable hosts.

q: Which of the following is NOT true about UDP?
options: It provides in-order delivery of datagrams
It supports an optional checksum for error detection
exp: UDP does not guarantee ordering or delivery; those are TCP features.

q: Which transmission medium is immune to electromagnetic interference?
exp: Optical fibre carries light, not electrical signals, so it is not affected by EMI.

q: In which switching technique are the packets of one message routed independently and may arrive out of order?
exp: In datagram switching each packet is routed independently, so packets can take different paths and arrive out of order.

q: Using the CRC generator polynomial x³ + x + 1 (1011), what is the CRC to be appended to data 1101?
exp: Dividing 1101000 by 1011 (mod-2) leaves remainder 001, so the transmitted word is 1101001.

q: Which layer of the TCP/IP model corresponds to the network layer of the OSI model?
exp: The Internet layer (IP) of TCP/IP corresponds to the OSI network layer.

q:
Match the protocol with its default port.
P. SMTP  Q. POP3  R. FTP (control)  S. DNS
1. 110  2. 21  3. 53  4. 25
exp: SMTP uses 25, POP3 uses 110, FTP control uses 21 and DNS uses 53.

q: Which traffic-shaping technique sends packets into the network at a constant rate irrespective of how bursty the arrival is?
exp: Leaky bucket outputs at a fixed rate; extra packets wait in the bucket or are discarded. Token bucket, by contrast, permits bursts.

q: A noiseless channel has a bandwidth of 4 kHz and uses 8 signal levels. What is the maximum bit rate by Nyquist's theorem?
Which field of the TCP header is used by the receiver to implement flow control?
exp: The receiver advertises its available buffer space through the window size field.

q: How many point-to-point links are required to connect 8 nodes in a fully connected mesh topology?
Which of the following is the IPv4 loopback address?
exp: The 127.0.0.0/8 block is reserved for loopback; 127.0.0.1 is the standard address.

q:
Assertion (A): Wireless LANs use CSMA/CA instead of CSMA/CD.
Reason (R): A wireless station cannot reliably detect collisions while it is transmitting.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
exp: Transmit and receive power levels differ greatly, so collision detection is impractical; hence collision avoidance is used.

q: A Go-Back-N protocol uses 3-bit sequence numbers. What is the maximum sender window size?
exp: For Go-Back-N the maximum window is 2ⁿ − 1 = 2³ − 1 = 7.

q: Which device can interconnect networks that use different protocols and architectures?
exp: A gateway performs protocol conversion and can connect dissimilar networks.

q: HDLC bit stuffing is applied to the data 0111111 (flag = 01111110). What is transmitted?
exp: After five consecutive 1s the sender inserts a 0: 0 11111 [0] 1 = 01111101, so the data can never imitate the flag.

q: DHCP servers listen for client requests using which transport protocol and port?
exp: DHCP uses UDP; the server uses port 67 and the client uses port 68.
